scene_script_excerpt:
SCENE 03 — Lightning ignites dry wood — 9 seconds
Setting and framing: Low three-quarter medium-wide source view of a dry dead tree beneath broad storm clouds, trunk near x=52% and lower branch near x=65%, y=62%. Keep sky for the strike and readable ground depth. Both raw endpoints retain the same camera view. The controlled 100%-to-110% push belongs in editing only.
Lighting: At the start use cool diffuse storm daylight only: slate blue-gray clouds, desaturated teal distance and cool brown wood. No fire or warm firelight exists before ignition. After ignition retain the cool ambient light with only a tiny warm reflection at the burning patch.
Camera: shot_size: Stable medium-wide source; closer presentation through editorial push.; height_and_angle: Low three-quarter side view, unchanged axis.; movement: Generation: stable low three-quarter medium-wide camera for the strike and ignition.; editing: Editing only: after a brief matching opening, make one controlled digital push from 100% to 110%, anchored near x=65%, y=62%, then hold. Keep the burning branch visible. Generate no additional zoom; raw endpoint assets remain uncropped. Keep the digital move smooth over stepped source footage; enforce source-state pairs first and check crops throughout the full move.; start_view: Trunk x=52%; dry branch/strike point near x=65%, y=62%; sky visible.; end_view: Same generated source crop; edited presentation ends at 110%.
First frame: The tree and dry lower branch are completely unlit. No lightning, flame, embers or firelight are visible. The empty woodland has no characters.

Sol: “Like when lightning hits a tree?”
Narrator: “Yes. Lightning's heat can set dry wood alight.”

Action: Hold the unlit tree and rigid dry branch for the opening off-screen question and Arthur's Yes. At about 3.8 seconds, one fixed complete painted lightning bolt briefly joins the sky to the dry branch for a single two-frame pair, then disappears completely. It does not travel or sweep. A small flame catches at that contact after the strike. Anchor its base to that ignition point; only small upper shapes change. Keep the tree, branch and cool storm background stable. No firelight in the unlit opening and no whole-scene brightness pulse.
Narrator attention: {"required": false, "gaze_target": null, "timing_status": "Actual saved voice takes measured at 1x; exact onsets in audio/voice-cues.json.", "final_voice_alignment_verified": false, "reason": "Sol is off-screen during Narrator speech."}
Last frame: The same source view of the tree and woodland. A small faceless painted flame burns at a newly darkened patch on the dry lower branch. The lightning is gone. Preserve branch attachments and cool storm light, with only faint local warmth beside the flame. The flame base is fixed to the ignition patch; the bolt is completely absent, the branch is rigid and no global brightness pulse is present.
Next cut: Cut to a separate time/place for ember tending in Scene 04; do not imply that this particular branch or fire is tracked across the cut.
